draft.title: Business support services
card: Business support services are people and groups outside the business that give a new owner advice and help. They can help the owner avoid costly mistakes.
lawyers advise on contracts, leases and legal duties. Accountants advise on record keeping, tax and budgets.
an IT provider can set up a website, online payments or computer systems, so the owner does not have to learn it all alone.
community groups, business networks and mentors share local knowledge, contacts and experience. A mentor is an experienced person who guides the owner, often for little or no fee.
draft.remember: Outside help gives a new owner skills and advice they may lack, and can save them from costly mistakes.

a.q: Which is the best example of a business support service for a new owner?
opts: An accountant advising on tax and record keeping
A bank lending the owner money to start
A customer buying a product from the owner
A new worker hired to serve customers
a.why: An accountant is an outside expert who gives advice that helps the owner avoid mistakes. The bank loan is a source of finance, not advice. Customers and employees are part of running the business, not outside support.
a.clue: Look for outside advice or help, not money or sales.

b.q: Tariq is opening a bike repair shop in Ballarat. He is about to sign a five-year lease and is unsure what the terms mean. Which support service should he use first?
opts: A lawyer, to explain the lease before he signs
An IT provider, to build a website for the shop
A mentor, to help him choose a shop name
A business network, to find extra customers
b.why: A lawyer advises on contracts and leases, so can show Tariq what he is agreeing to and help him avoid a costly mistake. A website or customer contacts may help later, but they do not answer his problem about the lease.
b.clue: Which service advises on contracts and leases?

a.best: An accountant advising on tax and record keeping

b.best: A lawyer, to explain the lease before he signs
